headline: High-risk shared filesystem/MCP pairing: Gemini CLI can write and modify git state while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can write repo files and use MCP; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes stdin/stdout and APIs. That creates a plausible content bridge where Gemini-produced files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions by OpenBB, even though no direct shared channel is documented beyond filesystem/MCP.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or MCP payload that OpenBBTerminal later parses as instructions
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server without provenance tracking
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers between the two agents
Use separate workspaces and mount points
Require manual review of any file or MCP output before OpenBB consumes it
Strip instruction-like text from Gemini-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI reads files in the cwd and has broad network egress; OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers. If they share a workspace, Gemini can read data OpenBB touches, and OpenBB can expose sensitive financial content through its outputs or API calls. The shared filesystem path is enough to make leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or mounted workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal loads sensitive financial or licensed data into files that Gemini CLI can read
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace
Restrict Gemini CLI to non-sensitive directories
Disable or proxy outbound API calls for OpenBBTerminal
Rotate any secrets present in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and exposes API/server surfaces. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes and state changes can collide, and Gemini's git mutations can race with OpenBB-generated artifacts. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict risk is default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF OpenBBTerminal persists outputs while Gemini CLI modifies git state in the same tree
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Review and commit changes manually
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs and act as a financial-modeling tool. If OpenBB treats Gemini output as authoritative, a bad suggestion can cascade into incorrect financial outputs or downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests Gemini-generated files, prompts, or MCP outputs without independent validation
IF Gemini CLI produces analysis that OpenBBTerminal renders or operationalizes
mitigations: Require human review before OpenBB acts on Gemini output
Add a validation step for all Gemini-produced facts
Limit Gemini to drafting only, not execution
Log source provenance for imported outputs
requires-engineering: implement schema and citation checks before action

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If regulated or licensed financial data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches through Gemini's filesystem access and OpenBB's API/server surfaces. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is stored in files accessible to Gemini CLI
IF OpenBBTerminal's API/server logging retains data longer than the operator expects
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Review retention settings for OpenBB APIs and logs
Use redacted datasets for Gemini-assisted work
Separate environments by jurisdiction if needed
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both tools
